A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Sum-of-Parts work and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D. The additional bibliography page in v5 shifts appendix pagination without preventing reliable comparison.

before.justification: v4 reports original benchmark experiments on ImageNet-S, CosmoGrid, and MultiRC, alongside ablations, probing, human evaluation, and cosmological analyses.

after.justification: v5 retains original SOP benchmark experiments, ablations, probing results, human evaluation, and cosmological analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, Section 3, and Appendix B retain the same group generator, frozen backbone, sparse group selector, binary masking, and gradient-passing loss scaling.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ImageNet/ImageNet-S classification, CosmoGrid cosmological regression, MultiRC reading comprehension, and human-evaluation coverage. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main experiments and appendices, including FastShap-F, ViT-Shapley-F, and AutoGnothi-F in Table A9. The newly cited concurrent SANN work is not evaluated.

E3.justification: Reported data selections, backbones, training schedules, computational budgets, metrics, perturbation procedures, and human-study design remain unchanged. The additional evaluation criteria discussed in Section 5 are literature context, not new experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same sparsity and group-count ablations, CosmoGrid threshold sensitivity, alternative occlusion and step-size tests, group-mask probing, and debugging and cosmology analyses.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting is unchanged, including the human-study standard deviations obtained through 1,000 bootstrap resamples in Appendix C.4.6. Adding the MTurk citation year does not indicate additional runs or participants.

E6.justification: Table 1 changes the MultiRC BERT backbone error from 0.682 ± 0.021 to 0.318 ± 0.021, now below SOP's unchanged 0.366 ± 0.021. This is a single revised result entry; other numerical results and plotted findings, including the appendices, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 and Appendix A retain the same insertion/deletion definitions, polynomial lower bounds, group-based zero-error theorems, proofs, and alternative mean-square-error derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about theoretical barriers, model-agnostic learning of feature groups, state-of-the-art SANN performance, and utility for debugging and cosmological discovery.

C2.justification: Interpretations of deletion-test bias, masking risks, group information leakage, model debugging, and cosmological findings are unchanged. The human-study uncertainty discussion and qualifications about realistic cosmological noise also remain.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same model identifiers, hyperparameters, training durations, hardware, data-processing details, and code/data access information in the main text and Appendices B-C.

R1.justification: Section 5 adds concurrent SANN work by Bassan et al. (2025), plus references on stability by Xue et al. (2024), contiguity by Kim et al. (2024), and minimality by Bassan and Katz (2023). These modestly broaden research positioning.

P1.justification: Section 5 gains short literature passages and streamlines sentences about prototype/concept models and coherence. Citation-year and version-date edits are also present, while the overall section structure and narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Expanded related work causes limited text reflow and moves Figure 8 upward within page 9. References spill onto an additional mostly blank page. Existing figure content, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Section 5 improves scholarly context by acknowledging concurrent SANN research and adding relevant explanation-evaluation literature, while local rewrites improve clarity. The unexplained Table 1 revision alone does not establish better experimental quality. With the method, proofs, and appendix evidence otherwise unchanged, the supported overall gain is modest.
